empty_file.jpeg.handwriting_by: mahir (grid lines only — a ruler-and-pen redraw of marks-grid-template.docx, no values filled in)
empty_file.jpeg.note: First real photo. Detection-only test (step 1) — no values were written, so this does not exercise step 2/3 recognition. Required KERNEL_DIVISOR 30->20 in detection.py to stop handwritten label-cell letters ('ID', 'Serial') from aliasing as column-divider lines — see learn.md step 1.

filled_file.jpeg.note: Second real photo, first with real values written in. Detection alone (step 1) required a second fix: a handwritten '1' in the tall Total cell (answer row, written '11') was tall enough to alias as a column divider, same failure mode as empty_file.jpeg's label text but from a digit instead of a letter. Fixed by requiring a candidate line to cover most of the table's own height/width (MIN_LINE_COVERAGE_FRAC), not just be locally the tallest thing — see learn.md step 1. Recognition (step 2/3, reading these digits) is not built yet; this entry only exercises geometry.

phone_2632711_1.jpg.handwriting_by: mahir (same physical script as filled_file.jpeg, re-photographed on a phone for step 6/7's real-device test session)
phone_2632711_1.jpg.note: First of 7 real phone captures from the step 6/7 live test session (2026-08-26), pulled from backend/debug_uploads/ (20260826T170044742283.jpg) after the user confirmed the correct student ID by hand. Only student_id is trustworthy ground truth here — it was given directly by the user. Serial/marks are deliberately left blank rather than transcribed from the photo: visually reading these same-script retakes turned up inconsistent serial values across supposedly-identical shots (e.g. phone_2632711_5.jpg's serial cell reads '107', not '07' like the others), which isn't something to guess into a ground-truth file. id_ocr_accuracy.py only needs student_id and skips entries without it, so this is enough to widen the ID-recognition sample beyond n=1.

KNOWN ANOMALY: Q4's ground-truth value (7) exceeds its own column's max (5) -- sum(marks) still equals the stated total (27), so this is a real marking-error on the original script, not a transcription slip. No legal-value-constrained decoder can ever match 7 for a max-5 question -- this field is structurally unscorable as "correct", not a bug to fix. Kept as-is because it's a genuine, valuable illegal-value test case (the app should flag/reject it, never store 7).

real_class_11.jpeg.note: Real photo #11 from a batch of 18 real class scripts (CSE211L pilot), transcribed ground truth in ../testset/real_class_info.json. Genuinely different student/writer per photo -- the first real multi-writer batch this test set has had beyond the single-writer phone/pen photos and the synthetic set. CORRECTION after a second detection fix round: this photo's own ID row genuinely has only 7 detected columns (one internal divider not found), not 8 -- a real, separate line-detection gap, unrelated to the adjacent-scripts-in-frame issue. It was initially (wrongly) reported as passing because a decoy candidate (the next script's own ID row, visible below this photo's marks table) happened to have the expected 8 columns and got silently substituted -- fixed by selecting id/serial by *position* relative to the marks table rather than by column count, so this genuine shortfall now surfaces honestly as column_count_mismatch instead of a false ok on the wrong student's ID. Left unfixed (not chased further) -- a real, known, documented gap, not guessed around.
